items.item:
1. In a log whose entries are all older than today, erasing before today
   leaves exactly the new erasure entry.
   Shows A15-2. [witness: verification:registry_a15_erase_before_today_leaves_only_own_entry]
statements:
```text
for entries e1 written before e2: e1.sequence < e2.sequence   -- A15-1
erase(d) accepted => no entry with instant < start_of(d) remains   -- A15-2
erase(d) accepted => its erasure entry e has e.instant >= start_of(d)   -- A15-3
```

verdicts.item:
1. In a log whose entries are all older than today, erasing before today
   leaves exactly the new erasure entry.
   Shows A15-2. [witness: verification:registry_a15_erase_before_today_leaves_only_own_entry]
statements:
```text
for entries e1 written before e2: e1.sequence < e2.sequence   -- A15-1
erase(d) accepted => no entry with instant < start_of(d) remains   -- A15-2
erase(d) accepted => its erasure entry e has e.instant >= start_of(d)   -- A15-3
```
verdicts.why: The check establishes that all prior entries are older than DAY_1, erasure leaves exactly one persisted entry, and that entry is the new erasure entry dated DAY_1, asserting A15-2 and A15-3. It only compares the erasure entry's sequence with the last old entry, so it does not assert A15-1 for every ordered pair of written entries.
